Fever will be responsible for key operational areas across multiple first-division football clubs, including ticketing, access control and box office operations . The role will oversee operations across multiple venues and will work closely with Venue Managers and experienced freelance operational leads assigned to each stadium. Your responsibility will be to ensure that each venue is properly prepared, that the onsite teams are operating according to Fever standards, and that operational issues are identified and resolved quickly. This is a hands-on coordination and problem-solving role . You will not necessarily be the person performing every operational task yourself. Instead, you will act as the operational reference for the people running each venue, stepping in whenever they need support or when something falls outside the standard process. Ensure each venue is operationally ready before doors open, including ticketing, access control, box office, devices, connectivity, staffing and processes. Monitor the overall performance of each venue and identify potential issues before they affect attendees or the partner. Ensure operational standards are applied consistently across all stadiums. Supervision of Venue Managers & Freelancers Brief and coordinate Venue Managers and experienced freelance operational leads. Distinguish between issues that can be solved locally and those requiring support from central Fever teams. Ensure escalations are clearly documented and followed through to resolution. Remain calm and decisive when unexpected problems occur during live operations. Operational Excellence Ensure Fever checklists, SOPs and tools are followed consistently. Identify recurring issues across venues and propose improvements to the central operations team. Capture learnings from each matchday and use them to improve future execution. Support the rollout of new processes, tools and operational standards across the network. What we are looking for: +4 years of experience in live operations, sports, ticketing, venues, hospitality or another high-volume operational environment. Experience coordinating onsite teams or multiple operational stakeholders. Proven ability to troubleshoot operational issues independently. Comfortable supervising experienced people without necessarily being their formal line manager. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Confident communicator with both operational teams and external partners. Comfortable working with operational technology and learning new systems quickly. Native Korean and strong professional English. Willingness to work evenings, weekends and travel regularly across South Korea. Benefits & Perks: Attractive compensation package and the potential to earn a significant bonus for top perfomance. review_candidates.title: Korean Medical Interpreter
review_candidates.description: Company Description Grupo Noa International is a premier virtual call center serving the international direct response industry. The company operates in a multilingual environment, supporting languages such as English, Spanish, French, Korean, and many others. Grupo Noa International currently answers customer service calls in over 29 countries, offering global exposure and diverse client interactions. The organization specializes in inbound customer service, outbound lead generation, upselling on service calls, and support for direct response campaigns. Team members work remotely, contributing to a flexible and distributed workforce. Role Description This full-time remote role is for a Korean Medical Interpreter supporting patients, healthcare professionals, and client organizations. The interpreter will provide accurate and culturally sensitive real-time interpretation between Korean and English during medical consultations, follow-up calls, and patient support interactions. Daily tasks include listening carefully to speakers, conveying meaning and intent in both languages, and ensuring that medical information, instructions, and consent details are clearly understood. The interpreter will also assist with occasional written translation of medical documents or patient communication, maintain confidentiality in accordance with healthcare privacy regulations, and adhere to company quality standards and call center protocols. Collaboration with supervisors and team members to improve service quality, participate in training, and follow established scripts or guidelines is also part of the role. Qualifications Strong skills in Medical Interpretation, Interpreting, and Simultaneous Interpretation in Korean and English. Ability to accurately use Medical Terminology in both Korean and English, with clear understanding of clinical and healthcare contexts. Competence in Translation of short medical documents or patient communications when required. Fluency in spoken and written Korean and English, with excellent listening and communication skills. Previous experience in medical or healthcare interpreting, call centers, or customer service is preferred. Familiarity with patient confidentiality standards and healthcare privacy regulations (e.g., HIPAA or equivalent) is an advantage. Reliable high-speed internet connection, suitable remote work environment, and ability to work full-time scheduled shifts. Relevant certification or training in medical interpreting or language services is a plus.
